title: bonsai.logs/1
description: bonsai logs and bonsai log append, with --json (contract §8, spec §8, §16 row 30): the log files of the main checkout's .bonsai/local/log/, or one file's records, or the record log append just wrote. Printed, never stored (the log itself is the log records, bonsai.log/1, one JSON line each). Written by those commands with --json; read by agents, the studio's forwarder and bridge, and CI, now that Bonsai has no screens of its own. bonsai logs lists the files (files filled, records null); bonsai logs for one file or session gives its records (files filled with that file, records filled); bonsai log append gives written. The records inside are bonsai.log/1's, as written; they are open objects here, because the schema checker has no $ref and a full copy would refuse an older or hand-written record, so bonsai.log/1 is their home. When the command refuses (exit 2 or 4), workspace is null, files and records and written are null, and error says why. A writer writes every field below, in this order, null, [] or {} where it does not apply (contract §2.2); a reader treats a missing field as null, keeps an unknown one and refuses a duplicate key.

format.description: The version, always the first field (contract §2.2).

workspace.description: The workspace: its id and name from bonsai.yaml, and the checkout's absolute path, forward slashes (printed locally, never stored or forwarded); null when the command stopped before reading bonsai.yaml.

root.description: The checkout's absolute path, forward slashes.

files.description: The log files, oldest first (a session's by its first record, a day file by its day), with what each holds; [] for a log with none; null when the command gave no list (log append, or a refusal).

file.description: The log file's name in .bonsai/local/log/: s-<session>.ndjson for a session, w-<YYYY-MM-DD>.ndjson for the records outside one (contract §8.5).

session.description: The session's id, for a session's file; null for a day file.

day.description: The UTC date, for a day file; null for a session's file.

first.description: The first readable record's time, as the log writes it; null when the file holds none.

last.description: The last readable record's time; null when the file holds none.

records.description: How many records were read from the file.

unreadable.description: How many lines were skipped as unreadable (a torn line a crash left): counted, never an error.

ended.description: For a session's file: true when its last span has ended (a session_end record, or a span old enough to count as ended), false while it is open; null for a day file.

task.description: For a session's file: the task its session_start record found (contract §13), or null; null for a day file.

role.description: For a session's file: the role its session_start record names, or null; null for a day file.

records.description: One file's records, as written (bonsai.log/1, which is their home), in file order; null when the command gave none.

written.description: The record log append just wrote (an event record, as written: bonsai.log/1); null when the run wrote none.

error.description: null unless the command refused or failed: then what went wrong and the next step, as bonsai.error has it.

examples.message: bonsai.yaml is not in this checkout, so it is not linked to Bonsai

next.do: run: bonsai init in the project's main checkout

code.description: What went wrong, as a fixed word: an open list (contract §2.2). Later steps add words, which is an addition (format review 4.5), and a reader shows a word it does not know as other. The known words live in one table in Bonsai's code, their one home, which bonsai check --schema bonsai.error prints (and, from step 5.1.10, the reference page of lists, docs/reference/lists.md); this schema does not copy them, and the words in its examples are illustrative.

message.description: What is wrong, one sentence for a person, in ASCII (spec §3).
examples: no --yes, and no terminal to ask at: nothing was written

next.description: The next thing to do (spec §3: every refusal and error names it, in the human line and in the JSON): what to do and who does it.

do.description: What to do: the command to run, written run: and the command line, or the step in plain words.
examples: open Claude Code in this checkout and accept its trust question

who.description: Who does it, a closed list: agent (any agent may do it, unattended) or person (a person's step: a consent such as --allow-exec, a tap, a setting, an install, or a command an agent's task does not grant it; spec §4, §6).
